evidence: The film thicknesses and the microstructures of Cu seed layers deposited on the 32-nm trench substrate were analyzed using scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM; Hitachi HD2300A). Sheet resistance was measured with a four-point probe (JANDEL) and Hall measurement system (Ecopia HMS-3000). High-resolution X-ray diffraction (XRD; Rigaku D/max-2500/pc, CuKα = 1.54062 nm, Japan) analysis was applied to study the crystallinity. The surface structure, morphology, and roughness of ALD Cu thin films were studied by field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM; JES 6340F, JEOL; operating voltage = 10.00 kV) and atomic force microscopy (AFM; Seiko Instrument SPA-400) in tapping mode. The impurities of the thin films were measured by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS; SIGMA PROBE, Thermo VG). The adhesion of the Cu thin films to the Ta diffusion barrier layer was examined with a tape-test using 3 M Scotch tape.
